Let us build a theme web for the chapter, one idea at a time.

say.en: At the centre we write the title. Around it we hang the big ideas of the chapter.
Endurance: cold, altitude and illness test the writer.
Faith: Kailash draws pilgrims of several religions.
Nature is beautiful and dangerous at the same time.
Friendship: the writer depends on Tsetan and Norbu.
Meeting other cultures: nomads, pilgrims and local customs.
An inner journey: the trip changes how the writer sees himself.

explanation.en: A drokba is a nomadic herder; the kora is the walk around Kailash; the kiang is the wild ass seen on the plateau.

body.en: Middleton writes in the first person with vivid description of landscape, weather and people. He mixes factual information with personal feeling and gentle, self-mocking humour about his own discomfort. Local words such as kora, drokba and kiang give authentic colour.

problem.en: "Silk Road" is both a physical and a spiritual journey. Discuss.

steps.en: Introduction: a travelogue of a journey across western Tibet to Mount Kailash.
Physical journey: the Changtang, snowy passes, altitude sickness, Hor and Darchen.
Spiritual journey: the goal is the kora; the writer shares the pilgrims' sense of purpose.
Conclusion: hardship and faith together make the trip a test of body and spirit.

answer.en: A good answer shows the physical challenges of the route, then the spiritual goal of the kora around sacred Kailash, and concludes that the hardships give the pilgrimage its meaning.
